## 1. Verified narrative

### 1.1 One repository, four hundred and fifty-one dependencies

Chromium is not a monorepo: it is one git repository plus a declarative description of everything else it needs. That description is `src/DEPS`, a 5,188-line file in Python syntax that at commit f288fed6 (`chrome/VERSION` 156.0.8067.0, 18 September 2026) declares 451 dependency entries — 273 git, 147 CIPD and 31 Google Cloud Storage — carrying 153 CIPD packages and 87 GCS objects, together with 143 variables, 61 hooks, 9 `recursedeps`, 24 `allowed_hosts` and 49 root `include_rules` [src/DEPS, parsed with depot_tools/gclient_eval.Exec]. Only three kinds exist: "`gclient` supports three dependency types: git, gcs and cipd" [src/docs/dependencies.md:9-10]. The reader of that file is gclient, a "meta checkout dependency manager for Git" whose on-disk state is exactly three things: `.gclient` (the solutions, written by `gclient config`), `.gclient_entries` (a cache of what is checked out) and each module's `DEPS` [depot_tools/gclient.py:6-20].

The division of labour matters. `.gclient` is the user's, `DEPS` the project's, and `gclient sync` reconciles them. Because `fetch chromium` writes a solution with no `managed` key, the developer's `src` checkout is left alone after its first clone: gclient prints "unmanaged solution; skipping" and moves only the dependencies beneath it [depot_tools/fetch_configs/chromium.py:14-42; depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:1099-1104]. The sync ends by writing `src/build/config/gclient_args.gni`, holding exactly the 17 variables `src/DEPS` exports [src/DEPS:39-58; depot_tools/gclient.py:1612-1631], which `build/toolchain/siso.gni` and `build/config/chrome_build.gni` import [src/build/toolchain/siso.gni:3-14]. From there the build takes over: the second half of this topic — Goma, then reclient, then Siso — is what happens to the pinned toolchain once it is on disk.

### 1.2 How it got here

gclient is older than public Chromium. The Google Code project was created on 2008-07-15 and received "Initial checkin of gclient." on 2008-08-05 from Steven Knight; revision 3 the same day added a `.gclient` "for self-hosted development syncing", so solutions/DEPS were the model from day one [https://storage.googleapis.com/google-code-archive/v2/code.google.com/gclient/commits-page-1.json]. chromium/src's own `DEPS` predates even that public checkin: it was committed 2008-07-27 at svn r20, 22 lines and 7 deps, still pointing V8 at an internal repository [https://api.github.com/repos/chromium/chromium/commits/...], a month before the 2008-09-02 "Welcome to Chromium" launch [https://blog.chromium.org/2008/09/welcome-to-chromium_02.html]. Every "2012" in a gclient header is therefore a bump-on-edit artefact — the year was last bumped on 2012-01-18 in an unrelated CL, and the docstring "Meta checkout dependency manager for Git." dates from the 2016-10-17 removal of SVN and `File()` support [depot_tools local history, unshallowed]. The vocabulary arrived quickly: `deps_os` on 2008-10-29, `Var()`/`custom_vars` in January 2009, `hooks` in February 2009, `revinfo` in March 2009 [Google Code commit list; chromium/src svn r4138].

Three structural events shaped the present file. First, the SVN-to-git cut-over: the last `git-svn-id` commit is r291560 at 2014-08-22 23:58:33 UTC, and 36 minutes later Stefan Zager landed "Update DEPS with all git URL's. / The king is dead. Long live the king." (#291561); `.DEPS.git`, the generated companion born 2011-06-02, was deleted at #291563 [GitHub API single-commit JSON]. Second, conditions: `gclient_eval.py` was created 2017-05-09, per-dep `condition` landed 2017-06-06, and chromium/src converted between 2017-09-18 and 2017-10-02, after which gclient itself stopped understanding `deps_os` (2018-05-16) and merely rewrites any survivor into `checkout_<os>` conditions [depot_tools history; gclient_eval.py:572-686]. Third, the content types: CIPD deps appear between M66 and M70 in 2018, `Str()` by M90 (2021), `git_dependencies = 'SYNC'` at M118 (September 2023), and first-class GCS deps plus the `non_git_source` var between M124 and M126 (2024) [raw.githubusercontent.com DEPS at those tags]. The file grew accordingly — 685 lines / 74 deps at M40, 2,553/218 at M70, 4,125/350 at M80, 4,876/399 at M100, 5,671/482 at M116, a peak of 6,034/524 at M128, then 4,821/423 at M140 and 5,188/451 today, counted twice with `gclient_eval.Exec` and an independent `ast.parse` [raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/<tag>/DEPS; corrected by verification V01].

### 1.3 depot_tools: the tool belt and `fetch chromium`

depot_tools is installed once and put on PATH; its README names `fetch`, `gclient`, `git cl` and `roll-dep` as the important tools and describes `gn`, `autoninja`, `siso` and `ninja` as thin wrappers that locate binaries inside the checkout [depot_tools/README.md:10-33]. It requires Python 3.8+ (gsutil 3.9–3.13) and self-updates on every `gclient` invocation unless `DEPOT_TOOLS_UPDATE=0` [depot_tools/README.md:3-5,73-76; depot_tools/gclient:8-28]. It is also, recursively, a Chromium dependency: `src/third_party/depot_tools` is pinned in DEPS at 0306e468 — the exact revision of the clone used throughout this dossier — and a hook disables self-update for that copy so it stays pinned [src/DEPS:2211-2212; src/DEPS:4456-4466]. The wrappers bundle nothing: `gn.py` asks `gclient_paths` for the primary solution and runs `<src>/buildtools/<platform>/gn`, itself a CIPD dep [depot_tools/gn.py:5-12,40-52].

`fetch chromium` is only a recipe runner. `fetch_configs/chromium.py` returns a spec whose single solution is `{name: 'src', url: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git, custom_deps: {}, custom_vars: {}}`, and `GclientGitCheckout.init` runs `gclient config --spec …` followed by `gclient sync`, adding `--nohooks`, `--no-history` or `--with_branch_heads` as requested, then sets `diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty` [depot_tools/fetch_configs/chromium.py:14-42; depot_tools/fetch.py:142-166]. `fetch android`, `fetch ios` and `fetch chrome` are aliases re-invoking the same config with extra props [depot_tools/fetch_configs/android.py:14-21]. The newest addition, `fetch --git-cache` (June 2026), sets `cache_dir` and `cache_mode='bootstrap'` so the clone is seeded from the prebuilt GCS mirror and then detached from it [depot_tools/fetch.py:225-231,323-332]. The documented entry point remains `fetch --nohooks chromium`, with the caution that the cache is "~30 GB for Chromium" and the command takes "30 minutes on even a fast connection" [src/docs/linux/build_instructions.md:70-108].

### 1.4 The grammar: `.gclient`, DEPS, and why neither is executed

`.gclient` is Python-shaped data, not a program: `gclient_eval.ParseLocalConfig` accepts only literal assignments [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:699-774]. A solution carries `name`, `url`, `deps_file`, `managed`, `custom_deps`, `custom_vars`, `custom_hooks` and `protocol_override`; top-level keys add `target_os`/`target_cpu` (unioned with the host through `DEPS_OS_CHOICES`, linux→`unix`), `cache_dir`, `cache_mode` and root hooks [depot_tools/gclient.py:2160-2256; :2043-2059]. `managed` deserves its own sentence, because the folklore is wrong: `fetch chromium` has written `managed: False` explicitly since 2013-08-22, an attempt to flip gclient's own default in June 2016 was reverted three weeks later for breaking iOS release branches, and the durable flip to unmanaged-by-default only happened on 2026-06-16 [depot_tools history; depot_tools/gclient.py:2225,4366-4375].

DEPS is parsed, never executed. `gclient_eval.Exec` runs `ast.parse`, accepts only single-target assignments to plain names with no re-definition, and allows constants, lists, tuples, dicts without duplicate keys, `Str(...)`, `Var(...)` and `+`/`%` [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:483-534; :360-480]. Every string passes a `str.format`-style expansion of `{name}` placeholders through a `_SafeFormatter` that rejects attribute and item access — which is why CIPD package templates must be spelled `${{platform}}` [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:51-71; src/DEPS:1172]. `Var()` reads a variable; `Str()` wraps one so it is emitted verbatim into GN args instead of being evaluated as a condition [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:74-93; depot_tools/gclient.py:1626-1631]. Vars are evaluated first, then built-ins (`checkout_android`…`checkout_win`, `host_os`, `checkout_x64`…, `host_cpu`), then `.gclient` `custom_vars`, which may only override names that already exist; the effective precedence is DEPS vars < parents < built-ins < custom_vars [depot_tools/gclient.py:1898-1922; :1924-1940]. The whole result is validated against a `schema` declaring the legal keys, and a dep value may be `None`, `'url@revision'`, a git dict, a CIPD dict (`packages` with `version` or `version_file`) or a GCS dict (`bucket` plus `objects` with `object_name`, `sha256sum`, `size_bytes`, `generation`) [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:258-357; :181-236]. Conditions are their own whitelist language — `and`/`or`/`not`, `==`, `!=`, `in`, with string-valued variables recursively evaluated as expressions [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:777-892]; `deps_os` and `hooks_os`, when they survive anywhere, are folded into `checkout_<os>` conditions [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:572-686]. Chromium's file exercises all of it: 320 of the 451 entries are conditional and three git-dep spellings coexist [src/DEPS:322-332; :3342-3343; :3075-3076].

### 1.5 What `gclient sync` actually does

`CMDsync` parses options (with `--jobs` defaulting to `max(8, CPUs)`), `LoadCurrentConfig` walks up to the `.gclient` and validates through `.gclient_entries` that the cwd belongs to that checkout, and `RunOnDeps('update')` builds an `ExecutionQueue` [depot_tools/gclient.py:4769-4772; :5409-5414; :2786-2845]. The queue is dependency-aware rather than merely parallel: a `Dependency` starts only when its requirements — parent, all top-level solutions for second-level nodes, and any dep whose path is a prefix of its own — have finished, and never concurrently with another job on the same repository URL [depot_tools/gclient_utils.py:1047-1059; depot_tools/gclient.py:672-708]. It prints "Still working on:" after 60 s, a reminder that dates from 2014-04-08, and since 2026-04-16 a "STALL DETECTED: gclient has been silent for 5 minutes." diagnostic after 300 s [depot_tools/gclient_utils.py:977,1085; commit 442cbd6d5; corrected by verification V07].

Each dependency checks itself out, then — only if allowed to recurse — parses its DEPS, runs `pre_deps_hooks` and enqueues children. Recursion is capped at two levels ("Only solution level and immediate DEPS are processed", hard-coded on 2010-06-28); a `recursion = N` key in DEPS is ignored with a warning, and only `recursedeps` grants deeper parsing — nine entries in Chromium: angle, dawn, instrumented_libs, openscreen, devtools-frontend, clank, the internal optimization-guide, ios_internal and webpagereplay [depot_tools/gclient.py:2084-2086; :1106-1119; src/DEPS:5170-5188]. Children inherit the parent's condition, ANDed in [depot_tools/gclient.py:798-806].

The git mechanics live in `GitWrapper.update`. A fresh dep is cloned with `git clone --no-checkout --progress [--shared] <url> <tmpdir>` and the `.git` directory moved into place; `--no-history` instead does `git init` plus a depth-1 fetch, and HEAD is left detached [depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:1759-1809; :1742-1758; :1811-1821]. An existing dep first tries the submodule fast path — if the gitlink already equals the pinned hash nothing runs — then handles URL switches, fetches only when the SHA is not already local, and branches into five documented cases (detached HEAD, non-tracking branch, DEPS moved to a hash, fast-forward merge, branch switch needing `--force`) [depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:1109-1121; :1241-1266; :1198-1214]. Underneath sits `git_cache.Mirror`: a bare repo per URL, populated under a lock and re-bootstrapped from `gs://chromium-git-cache/v2/<name>/<n>.ready` snapshots when it is missing, empty or has more than 50 packs — and only ten googlesource hosts have snapshots [depot_tools/git_cache.py:182-201; :781-819; :137-171].

After the queue drains, and only then, gclient writes `gclient_args.gni` if it changed, removes orphaned directories recorded in the previous `.gclient_entries` (deleting only with `-D`, and restoring submodule mount points with `git restore`), runs a single `cipd ensure` for every package from every DEPS with a generated ensure file (`$ParanoidMode CheckPresence`, `$OverrideInstallMode copy`, `@Subdir` blocks) against chrome-infra-packages.appspot.com, and finally runs hooks [depot_tools/gclient.py:2895-2943; :2554-2766; depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:2352-2392]. GCS objects are fetched during the tree walk instead: `gsutil cp`, then verification of both `sha256sum` and `size_bytes`, auto-extraction of tar (with `tarfile.data_filter`) or zip, and three hidden marker files that record the hash, the extracted names and the first-class-GCS migration [depot_tools/gclient.py:3318-3410; :3114-3173]. Hooks are a flat list, root-first then depth-first; `pattern` is a documented no-op under git, so all of them run, and a failure exits with status 2 [depot_tools/gclient.py:1698-1729; depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:238-256]. On a default Linux x64 host the shape of the work is modest compared with the file: 154 of 273 git deps, 24 of 147 CIPD entries and 17 of 31 GCS entries are active, and only 13 of the 61 hooks run [src/DEPS parsed with default Linux builtins].

### 1.6 Pinning a toolchain in text

Chromium's compiler is not installed; it is pinned. `tools/clang/scripts/update.py` holds `CLANG_REVISION = 'llvmorg-24-init-7747-g62397f8b'` with `CLANG_SUB_REVISION = 29` [src/tools/clang/scripts/update.py:36-47], but since June 2024 nothing fetches clang from a hook: `src/third_party/llvm-build/Release+Asserts` is a first-class GCS dep in bucket `chromium-browser-clang`, conditioned on `not llvm_force_head_revision`, with 23 objects — six each for Linux_x64, Mac and Win and five for Mac_arm64, which has no runtime-library package — each with its own condition [src/DEPS:924-1091; corrected by verification V03]. GN then cross-checks the result: `config("clang_revision")` reads the `cr_build_revision` stamp shipped inside the tarball, parses `CLANG_REVISION` and `CLANG_SUB_REVISION` out of `update.py`, asserts equality with the message "Did you forget to gclient sync?", and does the same for rustc/crubit/bindgen against `third_party/rust-toolchain/VERSION` [src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn:1480-1592 (fetched at f288fed6)]. Rust is pinned in lockstep because rustc is built against the pinned LLVM — its package name is `<RUST_REVISION>-<RUST_SUB_REVISION>-<CLANG_REVISION>` [src/tools/rust/update_rust.py:69-86].

A roll is a two-file edit plus a mechanical DEPS rewrite. `upload_revision.py` resolves the newest LLVM commit, computes the revision with `git describe --long --abbrev=8 --match=*llvmorg-*-init`, patches both update scripts and fires the `*_upload_clang`/`*_upload_rust` bots [src/tools/clang/scripts/upload_revision.py:151-215]; `package.py` uploads to staging with `x-goog-if-generation-match:0`, so a reused hash silently skips the upload [src/docs/updating_clang.md:90-96]; a permissioned Googler promotes staging to production and runs `sync_deps.py`, which stats and hashes each object and calls `gclient setdep --revision=path@object,sha256,size,generation` [src/tools/clang/scripts/sync_deps.py:56-153]. The documented cadence is every two to four weeks, with dry-run packaging CLs from the gardener's cron [src/docs/clang.md:3-5; src/docs/clang_gardening.md:54-90].

Everything else follows the same pattern with different transports. GN, ninja, Siso, luci-go and CPython 3.11.9 are CIPD packages [src/DEPS:1169-1197; :2773-2791; :2344-2366]; clang-format binaries and the nine Debian bullseye sysroots are content-addressed GCS objects, the sysroot object name being literally the tarball's sha256 [src/DEPS:754-808; :637-752]; libc++ and friends are git sub-repos whose revision must also be copied into `buildtools/deps_revisions.gni` [src/DEPS:524-528; buildtools/deps_revisions.gni:5-9]; the NDK and Android SDK are conditional CIPD deps [src/DEPS:1847-1858]; Windows and macOS keep script-driven hooks [src/DEPS:4525-4538]. PGO profiles stay hooks on purpose, because they weigh about a gigabyte and change roughly four times a day [src/DEPS:4923-5027]. The version string is generated by one small script: the unconditional `lastchange` hook runs `build/util/lastchange.py`, which does `git log -1 --format=%H %ct` filtered by `^Change-Id:`, reads the `Cr-Commit-Position` footer and writes `LASTCHANGE=<sha>-refs/heads/main@{#N}` [src/build/util/lastchange.py:153-189; :772-796], and `build/util/version.py` combines that with `chrome/VERSION` (`MAJOR=156 MINOR=0 BUILD=8067 PATCH=0`) for every downstream `@KEY@` substitution [src/chrome/VERSION:1-4; src/build/util/version.py:33-88].

### 1.7 Editing DEPS programmatically

Because DEPS is parsed to an AST *and* a token stream, edits are surgical: `_NodeDict` keeps the tokens, `RenderDEPSFile` untokenizes them, and `_UpdateAstString` swaps one string token, preserving its quote character [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:895-909; :900-909]. `SetRevision` follows `Var()` indirection — a dep spelled `Var('v8_revision')` is rolled by rewriting the *variable* — and refuses multi-line or implicitly concatenated strings; `SetCIPD` strips a `'version:' + Var(...)` prefix; `SetGCS` may only change `object_name`, `sha256sum`, `size_bytes` and `generation`, and demands the same object count [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:1137-1151; :1076-1106; :1016-1043]. On top sit `gclient getdep` and `gclient setdep`; in SYNC or SUBMODULES state `setdep` additionally stages the gitlink with `git update-index --add --cacheinfo 160000,<rev>,<path>` and prints "Changes have been staged" [depot_tools/gclient.py:5266-5335]. `roll-dep` is the human wrapper: it refuses a dirty tree, resolves `--roll-to` (default `origin/HEAD`), calls `gclient setdep`, rewrites the single `Revision:` line of `README.chromium`, and commits a message headed `Roll <dep>/ <from[:9]>..<to[:9]> (N commits)` [depot_tools/roll_dep.py:239-276; :143-184]. Around them are `gclient revinfo` (`-s` writes a snapshot `.gclient` pinning every dep), `gclient flatten` (one hermetic DEPS), `gclient recurse`, `gclient runhooks` and `gclient gitmodules` [depot_tools/gclient.py:4931-4989; :4058-4110; :3933-4055].

Validation is layered and presubmit-shaped. depot_tools' `CheckForCommitObjects` enforces DEPS/gitlink parity in SYNC state, with hard-coded exemptions only for ANGLE's and Dawn's placeholder entries [depot_tools/presubmit_canned_checks.py:2875-3138; :3056-3066]. `src/PRESUBMIT.py` adds a reviewer requirement for new DEPS hooks, `gclient verify` for `allowed_hosts`, a ban on new `download_from_google_storage` hooks, the `libcxx_revision` equality check, and `CheckUnwantedDependencies` over added includes [src/PRESUBMIT.py:4050-4071; :8302-8330; :3555-3667].

### 1.8 The machines that do the editing

Almost nobody rolls by hand. AutoRoll — "a program which creates and manages DEPS rolls of a child project, eg. Skia, into a parent project, eg. Chrome" — listed 343 rollers on 2026-09-20, of which 158 target chromium/src main: the 152 whose parent is labelled "Chromium", the five AFDO rollers labelled "Chromium Main", and one labelled "Chromium main branch"; the remaining 30 target beta, stable, LTS, m109 and m114 branches [https://skia.googlesource.com/buildbot/+/main/autoroll/README.md:3-20; https://autoroll.skia.org/…/GetRollers; corrected by verification V05]. Modes are RUNNING, DRY_RUN, STOPPED and OFFLINE; strategies BATCH, N_BATCH (N=20) and SINGLE; defaults are a ten-minute cooldown and three CQ attempts per CL [autoroll/README.md:59-105]. The Go implementation deliberately avoids gclient — its own `deps_parser` rewrites the DEPS line and, when `git_dependencies` is SYNC or SUBMODULES, the gitlink too, uploading both through the Gerrit REST API [https://skia.googlesource.com/buildbot/+/main/go/depot_tools/deps_parser/…; version_file_common.go:259-283].

The traffic this generates is measurable. In the week 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-21, Gerrit merged 5,519 chromium/src changes across 22 branches, 4,513 of them on main; 940 (20.8%) were owned by the two Skia autoroll service accounts and 972 (21.5%) had subjects starting "Roll " [https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/changes/?q=project:chromium/src+status:merged…]. The gitiles log agrees commit-for-commit — the window is exactly `Cr-Commit-Position` #1697016..#1701528, and both the first and last commit of the week are rolls [https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+log/refs/heads/main]. Over four weeks the share is stable at 22.9% (3,893 of 16,973), peaking at 26.3% in the Labor-Day week because humans pause and rollers do not, and running 40–68% at weekends [gitiles four-week log]. Not every roll touches DEPS: 220 of the week's 940 roller commits are PGO-profile rolls that change one line of `chrome/build/<platform>.pgo.txt`, and 625 main commits (13.8%) touched DEPS at all, 591 of them roller-owned. Of 3,893 roll commits in four weeks, 3,428 (88%) carry a `Tbr:` footer and just 14 carry `Reviewed-by` [gitiles four-week log, footer counts]. The tree's own HEAD, f288fed6, is itself an internal roll of `clank/internal/apps` [src git log -1].

### 1.9 Submodules: stage one, forever

On 2 March 2023 Josip Sokcevic announced on chromium-dev that Chromium was "moving away from git dependencies being managed by gclient DEPS to native Git submodules", to "simplify tooling" and "unlock our long term vision of … getting the Chromium codebase with just git client" [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/weYzs3_WWts]. The design doc adds the concrete win — no more synthetic commit for `codesearch/chromium/src` — and defines three stages: submodules alongside DEPS (2023 Q2), submodules as the source of truth with git deps removed from DEPS (2023 Q4), and, aspirationally, git itself managing them [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NhgzGAaApCds2yEhtnDDGoXeCc…]. The mechanism doc introduced the `git_dependencies` key with its three states and the custom `gclient-condition` key that native git ignores, and was candid that SUBMODULES mode breaks branch/HEAD pins, variable-based overrides and selective recursion [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1N_fseFNOj10ETZG3pZ-I30R__w…; depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:20-24]. Stage 1 landed on 23 August 2023 in commit ef72622958e9, adding `.gitmodules`, 231 gitlinks and `git_dependencies = 'SYNC'`, with M118 the first release branch to carry it [https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/ef72622958e9]. The rollout was rough — within hours developers reported submodules showing as uncommitted changes and `git cl upload` failures, and depot_tools spent months adding `gclient gitmodules`, `gclient installhooks`, `diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty` and `fetch/push.recurseSubmodules=off` [chromium-dev thread; depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:888-926].

Three years later the tree is in the same state, and exactly consistent: 273 git deps, 273 `.gitmodules` sections, 273 gitlinks, zero mismatches, plus the vestigial `SUBMODULE_MIGRATION` var no depot_tools code reads any more [src/DEPS + src/.gitmodules + `git ls-files -s`; src/DEPS:580-582]. The obstacles are documented rather than mysterious: the FAQ's own "Lots of Chromium infrastructure already parse DEPS file directly" [src/docs/git_submodules.md:249-253], 49 `*_revision` vars that `.gitmodules` cannot express [src/DEPS:340-444], `recursedeps` with no git equivalent (the `gclient-recursedeps` key is written but never read, and Chromium's `.gitmodules` contains none) [depot_tools/gclient.py:1248-1249], `use_relative_paths` still defaulting to False, ANGLE's and Dawn's deliberately gitlink-less placeholder entries, and Cog, where `gclient gitmodules` is unsupported [depot_tools/gclient.py:3944-3948]. Only three Chromium-orbit repositories reached SUBMODULES, all infrastructure: infra_superproject on 2023-09-08, infra/infra on 2025-03-07 ("having infra in the SYNC state is pretty annoying for dev-ex") and luci-py on 2025-04-30 [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/infra/+/ffa3742fd56b]. And the advertised end state does not work yet: `git clone --recurse-submodules` parses Chromium's `.gitmodules` fine, but 85 of the 273 submodules are on chrome-internal and fail anonymously, 144 conditions are ignored, git recurses into 25 nested `.gitmodules` gclient never touches, and nothing outside git happens — no CIPD, no GCS, no hooks, no `gclient_args.gni` [src/.gitmodules host tally; local experiment].

### 1.10 The same algorithm on a bot

Continuous-integration builders do not run `fetch`. Every chromium/src builder is launched through the `infra/chromium/bootstrapper` executable, which pulls the tools/build recipe bundle at `refs/heads/main` and reads the builder's `properties.json` out of chromium/src itself; the 2026 tree generates 1,066 such files, 584 ci and 438 try [src/infra/config/generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg:17-37]. The recipe calls `prepare_checkout`, which forwards to `bot_update.ensure_checkout` with cwd `[CACHE]/builder`, and the resulting command line is `vpython3 -u bot_update.py --spec-path … --revision_mapping_file … --git-cache-dir [CACHE]/git --cleanup-dir … [--patch_ref …] --revision src@<sha>` with `CHROME_HEADLESS=1`, git trace variables and `DEPOT_TOOLS_UPDATE=0` [depot_tools/recipes/recipe_modules/bot_update/api.py:306-396]. Inside, the order is fixed: set `core.trustctime false`, read or create the git-cache epoch, wipe the workspace if `.dirty_bot_checkout` exists, then per solution `git cache populate` (only when the pin is missing or `--enforce_fetch`), `git clone --no-checkout --local --shared <mirror> src`, `git fetch origin <pin>`, `git checkout --force`, `git clean -dff`, write `.gclient`, and run `gclient sync --verbose --reset --force --upstream --nohooks --noprehooks --delete_unversioned_trees --revision src@unmanaged`, followed by `gclient revinfo -a --ignore-dep-type cipd --output-json` to build the manifest [bot_update.py, per section BU]. Every subprocess is watched by a 300 s `ps auxwwf` timer and a 1200 s stale-process killer.

Two builds captured on 2026-09-22 make this concrete. CI `Linux Builder` ran with a cold builder cache but a six-day-old git cache: populate fetched 188,439 objects in 1.7 minutes, checkout took 3.4 minutes, `gclient sync` 6.6 minutes (167 deps cloned `--shared` from the local mirror, one `cipd ensure`), and disk went from 167 GB to 192 GB of 290 GB [https://logs.chromium.org/… build 8669987184970100865]. The try compilator ran the same tool in 80 seconds on a warm cache with `--patch_ref …refs/changes/99/8424399/3`, applied as a fetch, a `git cherry-pick --keep-redundant-commits` and a `git reset --soft`. Two knobs that exist are not used: no chromium/src builder sets `clobber`, `no_history` or `shallow` (zero of 1,666 builder_spec entries), and `bot_update_experiments` — the only path by which `gclient sync --experiment no-sync` could reach a bot — appears in none of the 1,066 properties files, so the no-sync optimisation is dormant plumbing [generated properties.json parse; depot_tools/recipes/recipe_modules/bot_update/api.py:703-706]. All chromium/src bots use `CacheMode.SHARED`; the bootstrap mode added in August 2026 is selected only by the developer-facing `fetch --git-cache` [depot_tools/gclient.py:2189-2202].

### 1.11 How big is a sync, in bytes

The GCS side is exact because DEPS declares `size_bytes`: a default Linux x64 checkout activates 17 GCS entries with 46 objects totalling 917,327,049 bytes, dominated by the Meet GPU test bundle (276,997,227 B, the "~278MB" the DEPS comment warns of) and the Rust tarball (276,524,576 B); clang is only 63,156,692 B in two objects [src/DEPS parsed; src/DEPS:1220-1232; :1093-1104]. CIPD sizes are not in DEPS and had to be resolved live: the 26 active packages sum to 621,162,316 bytes, led by the JDK at 148,797,791 B [chrome-infra-packages ResolveVersion/GetInstanceURL + HTTP HEAD, 2026-09-22]. The git side is measurable through the public cache bucket: the latest chromium/src snapshot is 15,481,300,760 bytes in 46 files — seven packs capped at 2 GiB, 842 MB of `.idx`, a 58.7 MB commit-graph and a 3.0 MB packed-refs holding 47,639 refs — and the 148 active deps that have snapshots cover 142 distinct repositories worth 8,055,808,935 unique bytes [https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1/b/chromium-git-cache/o?prefix=…]. Adding up: about 25.1 GB of unique content (25.70 GB if you sum by checkout path, because JetStream is mirrored at three paths and Speedometer at five), of which the non-git part is 1,538,489,365 B — 6.1% of bytes for 41 of the 195 active entries. Six active deps have no snapshot and were not measured, so both totals are lower bounds; the `small` configuration comes to 24,530,447,411 B [computed; corrected by verification V02]. For comparison, a `--depth=1` clone of chromium/src moves 517,131 objects / 1.35 GiB, while `git ls-remote` reports 9,642,463 refs, 9,589,406 of them `refs/changes` that neither clone nor mirror fetches [local measurement 2026-09-22].

### 1.12 Goma, and what it taught the build

Goma was Google's distributed compiler service: "Goma hooks a compile request, and sends it to a backend compile server", so a build can run at `-j500`, with the backend caching results [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/goma/client/+/5de52a5ece34/README.md]. The client had two halves: `gomacc` — prepended to the compiler command or symlinked in "masquerade mode" — parsed the flags, serialised an `ExecReq` and handed it to `compiler_proxy` over a unix socket [goma client 5de52a5ece34]. `compiler_proxy` was a multithreaded daemon whose `CompileTask` ran INIT → SETUP → FILE_REQ → CALL_EXEC → FILE_RESP → FINISHED. SETUP ran Goma's own directive-level C preprocessor, which seeded a macro environment (about 4,000 entries on Linux, over 15,000 on Windows because of windows.h), evaluated `#if`/`#ifdef` with a condition stack, honoured `#pragma once`, include guards and `#include_next`, and inserted only the files a compiler would open [goma client; SI section]. FILE_REQ uploaded inputs as content-addressed `FileBlob`s, embedding files under 2 MB and chunking larger ones; CALL_EXEC sent the request over plain HTTP/1.1 with protobuf bodies to `goma.chromium.org/cxx-compiler-service` — the design EngFlow contrasted with RE-API's gRPC: "Goma uses plain HTTP/1, so it needs lots of connections, and files need to be broken into chunks" [https://blog.engflow.com/2023/09/11/goma-is-gone--put-everything-into-reclient/]. Hermetic mode defaulted to `error`, so the backend had to use a compiler with the same version string and binary hash or the task failed rather than silently compiling with a different binary.

The end came in stages. Goma's backend was RBE-backed by November 2020, making the Goma protocol a middleman; the same team wrote reclient, mirroring `gomacc`→`rewrapper` and `compiler_proxy`→`reproxy`, keeping Goma's include scanner as the `-gomaip` flavour [https://blog.engflow.com/…; https://github.com/bazelbuild/reclient]. On 8 September 2023 — the chromium-dev archive timestamp is UTC, so US Pacific readers date it 7 September — Takuto Ikuta posted "PSA:Goma deprecation" to infra-dev, chromium-dev and chrome-build-team: "Goma will be deprecated by the end of January of next year", Google would "delete support for goma in Chromium builds around the beginning of 2024" and "stop maintaining the goma client and server" [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/rajt7THxIng]. `gn gen` began warning on 2023-09-26, the last client roll landed 2023-09-27, autoninja started exiting for `use_goma` on Linux and macOS on 2024-02-13, and the `use_goma`/`goma_dir` args were deleted on 2024-05-15; on 2024-05-21 both repositories were reduced to a README reading "Goma is not maintained any more, please use reclient instead." Only fossils remain in 2026: the RBE project name `goma-foundry-experiments`, the `copy_staging_to_prod_and_goma.sh` name in the clang roll doc, and the `-gomaip` suffix [src/build/config/siso/configure_siso.py:20-22].

### 1.13 The 2026 stack: Siso first, reclient deprecated

Three GN args decide everything. `use_remoteexec` defaults to false; `use_siso` defaults to true whenever gclient has written `build/config/siso/.sisoenv`, `build_with_chromium` is set and the out dir has no Ninja `.ninja_deps`; and `use_reclient` is derived as `use_remoteexec && !use_siso` [src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:25-31; src/build/toolchain/siso.gni:5-22]. GN asserts that remote execution needs one of the two clients, rejects `cc_wrapper` and a custom `clang_base_path`, insists the out dir is exactly two levels deep or "remote cache hits are basically zero", and since November 2025 prints `WARNING: crbug.com/424659245 - Reclient is deprecated` whenever `use_reclient` is true [src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:56-69; src/BUILD.gn:1649-1656]. Its decisions are serialised into `out/<dir>/gn_logs.txt`, and that file — not `args.gn` — is what Siso's starlark reads [src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:71-81].

Reclient still exists, but barely: its binaries are downloaded only when `download_reclient` (default `checkout_chromeos`) is true, pinned at `re_client_version:0.185.0.db415f21-gomaip`, while depot_tools' own manifest keeps the older 0.124.1 build "only for ChromeOS build" [src/DEPS:297-307; depot_tools/cipd_manifest.txt:81-83; corrected by verification V06]. Where it runs, `rewrapper -cfg=<cfg> -exec_root=<root>` wraps every compile, `reclient_helper.py` brackets the build with `bootstrap --re_proxy=… --cfg=reproxy.cfg` and sets racing defaults (`RBE_local_resource_fraction=0.2`, `RBE_racing_bias=0.95`), and `reproxy.cfg` points at `remotebuildexecution.googleapis.com:443` with `depsscanner_address=exec://…/scandeps_server` [src/build/toolchain/gcc_toolchain.gni:199-200; depot_tools/reclient_helper.py:288-325; buildtools/reclient_cfgs/reproxy_cfg_templates/reproxy.cfg.template]. Even Siso-native builds on Windows and macOS still parse rewrapper cfgs for platform properties [src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:91-94].

Siso is a Ninja-compatible Go build tool with a built-in REAPI client, a digest-based filesystem and starlark configs, pinned in DEPS as CIPD `build/siso/${platform}` at `git_revision:22353054` [src/DEPS:291-292]. The unconditional `configure_siso` hook writes `.sisoenv` and copies a backend config — `google.star` for the eleven known Google RBE projects — which defines two platforms, `default` and `large`, on a pinned `siso-chromium/linux` image [src/DEPS:5100-5116; src/build/config/siso/configure_siso.py:92-112; backend_config/google.star:9-29]. `main.star` assembles the step config from gn args and `gn_logs.txt`, then layers rules per host and toolchain, and force-disables remote for everything unless `gn_logs` says `use_remoteexec=true` [src/build/config/siso/main.star:37-109]. Representative choices: clang compiles are remote with a 2 m timeout; links run on `large` with 10 m (80 m under ThinLTO) and never on darwin; mojom generators use `large` only under `googlechrome`, justified by a measurement (880 ms on n2-highmem-8 versus 2.43 s on n2-custom-2-3840); about seventy Python and node scripts are denylisted to local [src/build/config/siso/clang_unix.star:214-227; mojo.star:12-31; denylist.star:11-27]. Siso's limits are derived from the machine — step 512×CPUs, scandeps 2×, local = CPUs, remote 80×CPUs — and a remote-eligible step walks start-local, cache lookup, fast-local, remote execution, retry, then local fallback, except for auth and bad-image errors [Siso README/docs on go.chromium.org/build]. `autoninja` mirrors `siso.gni`'s logic, refuses to switch tools without `gn clean`, enforces account policy (rbe-chromium-untrusted may not build src-internal) and converts `-j` into `-remote_jobs` or `-local_jobs` [depot_tools/autoninja.py:157-231; :411-436]. On the bot side, 866 of the 1,066 generated builders carry `$build/siso` properties, and only five `*-build-perf-developer` builders still carry `$build/reclient` to A/B the old stack [src/infra/config/generated/builders/*/*/properties.json].

### 1.14 Where the two generations really differ: input discovery

The deepest difference is not the transport but how each system decides what to upload, because the input-root digest is half of the action digest [Siso docs]. Goma computed the exact set with a real preprocessor, cached parsed directive lists in an `IncludeCache` sized for 140,000 entries, and skipped the whole walk when a `DepsCache` entry keyed by a SHA-256 command identifier still validated by `FileStat` and directive hash [goma client; SI section]. Reclient kept that engine: `scandeps_server` is a gRPC `CPPDepsScanner` whose `-gomaip` flavour links the `infra/goma-input-processor` fork [https://github.com/bazelbuild/reclient/…]. Siso does the opposite. Its `scandeps` package calls itself a "forged" scanner that exists "to construct inputs for remote execution" and is "not used to check whether the action needs to re-execute"; it understands only `#include "x"`, `<x>` and `MACRO`, ignores `#if` entirely, and therefore expands *all* recorded values of a macro — a deliberate over-approximation [https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/scandeps/doc.go]. What keeps the superset cheap is the precomputed subtree: directories labelled `dir:headers` in `input_deps` are never scanned but attached as a Merkle `TreeEntry` digested once per build, with only the root digest probed against the CAS — a change benchmarked at 378.3 s → 373 s on a full build [siso/build subtree init; clang_all.star:48-72; mac_sdk.star:39-52]. Underneath, `hashfs` caches mtime/size/SHA-256 per file and persists to `.siso_fs_state`; on Cog/CartFS/ABFS the digest is not even computed locally but read from an xattr or fetched from the filesystem service [Siso hashfs docs]. One widely repeated claim is now false: "fast-deps", the feature that rebuilt remote inputs from the previous deps log, was deleted on 2026-04-10 because it is "not possible to know whether the cached dependency information is still safely usable"; the deps log today only drives the dirty check, and the successor — two-phase caching — is still gated behind `SISO_EXPERIMENTS=two-phase-caching`, which nothing in Chromium sets [https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/339149ef3d30].

### 1.15 The state of the union, September 2026

The system sits in a stable intermediate state on two axes at once. The dependency description is mid-migration — `git_dependencies = 'SYNC'`, three years after a stage 2 that was scheduled for 2023 Q4 and still has no revised ETA, with its tracking bug open and last touched in March 2025 [src/DEPS:35-37; https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40254050]. The build is mid-migration too — Siso is the default everywhere and reclient was announced for removal "at the end of September" 2025, yet the 2026 tree still ships its cfg plumbing, its hybrid mode and a CIPD pin [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/…; src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:29-31]. Both show the pattern that explains the whole topic: the declarative file is easy to change and the ecosystem around it is not, so Chromium keeps the old interface alive — DEPS for the rollers and parsers, rewrapper cfgs for Windows and macOS — while the new mechanism carries the load underneath.

| RS-F107 | Siso's default concurrency limits: step = 512×CPUs, scandeps = 2×CPUs, local = CPUs, remote = 80×CPUs (Intel Mac capped at 1000, Apple Silicon ×8), fastlocal = max(0,CPUs-32)/16 (min 1), and the rewrapper limit reuses autoninja's NINJA_CORE_MULTIPLIER logic; SISO_LIMITS overrides any of them. | https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/build/limits.go (lines 20-32, 61-76, 162-200) | stepLimitFactor = 512 ... scanDepsLimitFactor = 2 ... remoteLimitFactor = 80 ... // Intel Mac has bad performance with a large number of remote actions. if runtime.GOARCH == "amd64" { return min(1000, limit) } // Apple Silicon has better scalability than Intel. limit *= 8 | verified-web |
| RS-F108 | Siso's runRemote algorithm: run the first startLocal steps locally; check the remote cache using the deps log; run locally if local resources are idle (fast local); otherwise execute remotely with deps-log inputs, retry with a full deps scan, and finally fall back to local — each fallback type is counted and the build fails on TooManyFallbackError. | https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/build/run_remote.go (lines 27-40, 110-118, 145-156) | 1. for initial steps of startLocal, run locally. 2. Check remote cache with deps log if available. 3. If local resource is idle, run locally. 4. Otherwise, try running a remote execution with deps log. 5. If it failed, it will retry a remote execution with deps scan. 6. If it still failed, it will fallback to local execution. | verified-web |
| RS-F109 | Siso never falls back to local for PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated, InvalidArgument, FailedPrecondition, a bad platform container image, non-relocatable inputs, or a remote compile error that produced output; it does fall back on exit 137 (OOM/SIGKILL), deadline exceeded, slow scandeps and output flush errors. | https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/build/run_remote.go (lines 55-109) | case codes.PermissionDenied, codes.Unauthenticated, codes.InvalidArgument, codes.FailedPrecondition: return false, fmt.Errorf("remote-exec %s failed: %w", step.cmd.ActionDigest(), err) ... case eerr.ExitCode == 137: // we still see unexpected SIGKILL (OOM?) fallbackReport("fallback-on-SIGKILL") | verified-web |
| RS-F110 | A step is remote-eligible only if a remote executor exists and the step has platform properties; strategy is runRacing when the 'racing' experiment is enabled, else runRemote, else runLocal; racing runs local and remote in parallel and cancels the loser (mirroring reclient's racing). | https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/build/run_cmd.go (lines 14-18, 52-64); .../siso/build/run_racing.go (lines 34-40) | return (b.remoteExec != nil && len(step.cmd.Platform) > 0) ... case step.cmd.Pure && b.allowRemote(step) && b.racingEnabled: return b.runRacing / // runRacing runs a step with local and remote execution in parallel. // Whichever finishes first wins; the loser is cancelled. | verified-web |

"two-phase-caching": "", / // Experiments are enabled by SISO_EXPERIMENTS environment variable. // We don't guarantee experiment id in future versions. | verified-web |

| RS-F115 | Key Siso-vs-Ninja differences: Siso fails on missing inputs/outputs where Ninja is silent, expands foo.h^ to a source that includes it, locks the build dir against concurrent builds, fails on depfile parse errors, re-runs when the inputs/outputs list changes, and supports remote_enabled/remote_platform_ref/remote_timeout, restat_content, cache_disabled and directory inputs in .ninja files. | https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/docs/ninja_diff.md (lines 1-108) | * **Siso:** Enforces strict input dependency checks. If an input file is missing when scheduling a build step, Siso will fail the build. ... `remote_enabled`, `remote_platform_ref`, and `remote_timeout` can be used to control how the action is run remotely. ... * **Siso:** Locks the build directory | verified-web |
| RS-F116 | Reclient consists of rewrapper (forwards build commands to RBE), reproxy (long-lived process talking to RBE/CAS), bootstrap (starts/stops reproxy and aggregates metrics) and scandeps_server (include scanner started by reproxy); it is 'not an officially supported Google product'. | https://github.com/bazelbuild/reclient/blob/main/README.md (lines 28-42) | 1. **rewrapper** - a wrapper that forwards build commands to RBE 1. **reproxy** - a process that should be started at the beginning of the build and shut down at the end. ... 1. **bootstrap** - starts and stops reproxy, and aggregates the metrics during the shutdown. 1. **scandeps_server** - a standalone process for scanning includes | verified-web |
| RS-F117 | Reclient's exec_strategy values: local (local execution, remote caching), remote (fail if remote fails), remote_local_fallback (retry failing remote action locally), racing (start local too if remote is slow and local resources allow; first finisher wins); racing_bias defaults to 0.75 and exec_timeout to 1 hour. | https://github.com/bazelbuild/reclient/blob/main/docs/cmd-line-flags.md (lines 170-174, 282-284, 327-343) | * `racing` - If a remote action doesn't complete within a certain amount of time and there are sufficient local resources available, will start running the action locally as well. The results of the first to finish are used. ... Default is 0.75. ... The amount of time to allow this command to execute. The default is 1 hour. | verified-web |
| RS-F118 | Reclient is released to CIPD infra/rbe/client in two flavours per platform — Goma include scanner builds with a -gomaip version suffix (used for Chromium) and clang-scan-deps builds (-csd package suffix, used by Android); Goma's input processor is described as 3x faster than clang-scan-deps for a typical Chrome compile. | https://github.com/bazelbuild/reclient/blob/main/README.md (lines 116-118, 186-231) | Goma's input processor is 3x faster than clang-scan-deps for a typical compile action in Chrome. ... | RS-F120 | In the Remote Execution API an Action is identified by the digest of its wire encoding and consists of a command_digest and an input_root_digest (a Merkle tree of Directory messages in the CAS); the ActionCache maps that action digest to an ActionResult, which is what makes remote cache hits possible across machines. | https://github.com/bazelbuild/remote-apis/blob/main/build/bazel/remote/execution/v2/remote_execution.proto (lines 141-147, 653-687) | `Action`s can be succinctly identified by the digest of their wire format encoding and, once an `Action` has been executed, will be cached in the action cache. ... Digest command_digest = 1; ... Digest input_root_digest = 2; | verified-web |

### X1. `depot_tools/fetch_configs/chromium.py`:15-38

*Shows (DT):* The complete Chromium fetch recipe: solution dict, props for webkit ToT / internal / target_os, and the gclient_git spec type.

```python
    def fetch_spec(props):
        url = "https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git"
        solution = {
            "name": "src",
            "url": url,
            "custom_deps": {},
            "custom_vars": {},
        }
        if props.get("webkit_revision", "") == "ToT":
            solution["custom_vars"]["webkit_revision"] = ""
        if ast.literal_eval(props.get("internal", "False")):
            solution["custom_vars"]["checkout_src_internal"] = True
        spec = {
            "solutions": [solution],
        }
        if props.get("target_os"):
            spec["target_os"] = props["target_os"].split(",")
        if props.get("target_os_only"):
            spec["target_os_only"] = props["target_os_only"]

        return {
            "type": "gclient_git",
            "gclient_git_spec": spec,
        }
```

### X2. `depot_tools/fetch.py`:142-166

*Shows (DT):* GclientGitCheckout.init: gclient config --spec, gclient sync flags, tag fetch refspec and diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty.

```python
    def init(self):
        # Configure and do the gclient checkout.
        self.run_gclient("config", "--spec", self._format_spec())
        sync_cmd = ["sync"]
        if self.options.nohooks:
            sync_cmd.append("--nohooks")
        if self.options.nohistory:
            sync_cmd.append("--no-history")
        if self.spec.get("with_branch_heads", False):
            sync_cmd.append("--with_branch_heads")
        self.run_gclient(*sync_cmd)

        # Configure git.
        wd = os.path.join(self.base, self.root)
        if self.options.dry_run:
            print("cd %s" % wd)
        if not self.options.nohistory:
            self.run_git(
                "config",
                "--add",
                "remote.origin.fetch",
                "+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*",
                cwd=wd,
            )
        self.run_git("config", "diff.ignoreSubmodules", "dirty", cwd=wd)
```

### X5. `depot_tools/gclient_paths.py`:21-34

*Shows (DT):* FindGclientRoot walking up the directory tree looking for .gclient.

```python
def FindGclientRoot(from_dir, filename=".gclient"):
    """Tries to find the gclient root."""
    real_from_dir = os.path.abspath(from_dir)
    path = real_from_dir
    while not os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, filename)):
        split_path = os.path.split(path)
        if not split_path[1]:
            return None
        path = split_path[0]

    logging.info("Found gclient root at " + path)

    if path == real_from_dir:
        return path
```

```python
    entries_content = gclient_utils.FileRead(entries_filename)
```

```python
            return _convert(node.left) % _convert(node.right)
```

### X8. `depot_tools/gclient_eval.py`:543-567

*Shows (DT,SY):* Exec's ordering: vars first, then builtin_vars, then custom_vars overrides (existing keys only), then evaluation of every statement and schema validation. | Exec(): vars are evaluated first, builtin vars layered on, custom_vars overrides applied only for declared names, then every statement is evaluated and schema-validated.

```python
    # Process vars first, so we can expand variables in the rest of the DEPS
    # file.
    vars_dict = {}
    if "vars" in statements:
        vars_statement = statements["vars"]
        value = _gclient_eval(vars_statement, filename)
        local_scope.SetNode("vars", value, vars_statement)
        # Update the parsed vars with the overrides, but only if they are
        # already present (overrides do not introduce new variables).
        vars_dict.update(value)

    if builtin_vars:
        vars_dict.update(builtin_vars)

    if vars_override:
        vars_dict.update(
            {k: v for k, v in vars_override.items() if k in vars_dict}
        )

    for name, node in statements.items():
        value = _gclient_eval(node, filename, vars_dict)
        local_scope.SetNode(name, value, node)

    try:
        return _GCLIENT_SCHEMA.validate(local_scope)
```

### X10. `depot_tools/gclient_eval.py`:858-881

*Shows (DT):* EvaluateCondition's comparison rules: exactly one operator, ==, != or `in` (tuple RHS allowed only for `in`).

```python
        if isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
            if len(node.ops) != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    "invalid compare: exactly 1 operator required (inside %r)"
                    % (condition)
                )
            if len(node.comparators) != 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    "invalid compare: exactly 1 comparator required (inside %r)"
                    % (condition)
                )

            left = _convert(node.left)
            right = _convert(
                node.comparators[0], allow_tuple=isinstance(node.ops[0], ast.In)
            )

            if isinstance(node.ops[0], ast.Eq):
                return left == right
            if isinstance(node.ops[0], ast.NotEq):
                return left != right
            if isinstance(node.ops[0], ast.In):
                return left in right
```

### X12. `depot_tools/gclient_scm.py`:2352-2362

*Shows (DT,QP):* CipdRoot._create_ensure_file: the single ensure file ($ParanoidMode CheckPresence, $OverrideInstallMode copy, @Subdir groups) fed to `cipd ensure`. | how the 26 packages become one cipd ensure call (copy mode, two subdirs for cpython3)

```python
    def _create_ensure_file(self):
        try:
            contents = "$ParanoidMode CheckPresence\n"
            # TODO(crbug/1329641): Remove once cipd packages have been updated
            # to always be created in copy mode.
            contents += "$OverrideInstallMode copy\n\n"
            for subdir, packages in sorted(self._packages_by_subdir.items()):
                contents += "@Subdir %s\n" % subdir
                for package in sorted(packages, key=lambda p: p.name):
                    contents += "%s %s\n" % (package.name, package.version)
                contents += "\n"
```

*Shows (SY):* get_vars(): the variable precedence stack (DEPS vars < parents < built-ins < custom_vars).

```python
    def get_vars(self):
        """Returns a dictionary of effective variable values
        (DEPS file contents with applied custom_vars overrides)."""
        # Variable precedence (last has highest):
        # - DEPS vars
        # - parents, from first to last
        # - built-in
        # - custom_vars overrides
        result = {}
        result.update(self._vars)
        if self.parent:
            merge_vars(result, self.parent.get_vars())
        # Provide some built-in variables.
        result.update(self.get_builtin_vars())
        merge_vars(result, self.custom_vars)

        return result
```

```python
def UpdateCondition(info_dict, op, new_condition):
    """Updates info_dict's condition with |new_condition|.

    An absent value is treated as implicitly True.
    """
    curr_condition = info_dict.get("condition")
    # Easy case: Both are present.
    if curr_condition and new_condition:
        info_dict["condition"] = "(%s) %s (%s)" % (
            curr_condition,
            op,
            new_condition,
        )
    # If |op| == 'and', and at least one condition is present, then use it.
    elif op == "and" and (curr_condition or new_condition):
        info_dict["condition"] = curr_condition or new_condition
    # Otherwise, no condition should be set
    elif curr_condition:
        del info_dict["condition"]
```

```python
        # Structure git submodules into a dict of DEPS git url entries.

                path = module["path"]
            else:

            # TODO(crbug.com/1471685): Temporary hack. In case of applied
            # patches where the changes are staged but not committed, any
            # gitlinks from the patch are not returned by `git ls-tree`. The
            # path won't be found in commit_hashes. Use a temporary '0000000'
            # value that will be replaced with w/e is found in DEPS later.
            submodules[path] = {

                    module["url"], commit_hashes.get(module["path"], "0000000")
```

```python
    def _create_ensure_file(self):
        try:
            contents = "$ParanoidMode CheckPresence\n"
            # TODO(crbug/1329641): Remove once cipd packages have been updated
            # to always be created in copy mode.
            contents += "$OverrideInstallMode copy\n\n"
            for subdir, packages in sorted(self._packages_by_subdir.items()):
                contents += "@Subdir %s\n" % subdir
                for package in sorted(packages, key=lambda p: p.name):
                    contents += "%s %s\n" % (package.name, package.version)
                contents += "\n"
            ensure_file = None
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
                suffix=".ensure", delete=False, mode="wb"
            ) as ensure_file:  # noqa: F811
                ensure_file.write(contents.encode("utf-8", "replace"))
            yield ensure_file.name
        finally:
            if ensure_file is not None and os.path.exists(ensure_file.name):
                os.remove(ensure_file.name)
```

```python
    def GetHooks(self, options):
        """Evaluates all hooks, and return them in a flat list.

        RunOnDeps() must have been called before to load the DEPS.
        """
        result = []
        if not self.should_process or not self.should_recurse:
            # Don't run the hook when it is above recursion_limit.
            return result
        # If "--force" was specified, run all hooks regardless of what files
        # have changed.
        if self.deps_hooks:
            # TODO(maruel): If the user is using git, then we don't know
            # what files have changed so we always run all hooks. It'd be nice
            # to fix that.
            result.extend(self.deps_hooks)
        for s in self.dependencies:
            result.extend(s.GetHooks(options))
        return result
```

```python
    def _SaveEntries(self):
        """Creates a .gclient_entries file to record the list of unique checkouts.

        The .gclient_entries file lives in the same directory as .gclient.

        # Sometimes pprint.pformat will use {', sometimes it'll use { ' ... It
        # makes testing a bit too fun.
        result = "entries = {\n"
        for entry in self.root.subtree(False):
            result += "  %s: %s,\n" % (
```

*Shows (SY):* Mirror.UrlToCacheDir(): how a repo URL becomes a cache directory name.

```python
    def UrlToCacheDir(url):
        """Convert a git url to a normalized form for the cache dir path."""
        if os.path.isdir(url):
            # Ignore the drive letter in Windows
            url = os.path.splitdrive(url)[1]
            return url.replace("-", "--").replace(os.sep, "-")

        parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)
        norm_url = parsed.netloc + parsed.path
        if norm_url.endswith(".git"):
            norm_url = norm_url[: -len(".git")]

        # Use the same dir for authenticated URLs and unauthenticated URLs.
        norm_url = norm_url.replace("googlesource.com/a/", "googlesource.com/")

        norm_url = Mirror.URL_ALIASES.get(norm_url, norm_url)

        norm_url = norm_url.replace(":", "__")

        return norm_url.replace("-", "--").replace("/", "-").lower()
```

```python
def RenderDEPSFile(gclient_dict):
    contents = sorted(gclient_dict.tokens.values(), key=lambda token: token[2])
    return tokenize.untokenize(contents)


def _UpdateAstString(tokens, node, value):
    if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
        node = node.args[0]
    position = node.lineno, node.col_offset
    quote_char = ""
    if _IsStringConstant(node):
        quote_char = tokens[position][1][0]
        value = value.encode("unicode_escape").decode("utf-8")
    tokens[position][1] = quote_char + value + quote_char
    node.value = value
```

### X42. `depot_tools/roll_dep.py`:143-166

*Shows (PD):* roll-dep builds its 'Roll <dep>/ a..b (N commits)' header from git log, filtering earlier roll commits

```python
def generate_commit_message(
    full_dir, dependency, head, roll_to, upstream_url, show_log, log_limit
):
    """Creates the commit message for this specific roll."""
    commit_range = f"{head}..{roll_to}"
    commit_range_for_header = f"{head[:9]}..{roll_to[:9]}"
    cmd = ["git", "log", commit_range, "--date=short", "--no-merges"]
    logs = check_output(
        # Args with '=' are automatically quoted.
        cmd + ["--format=%ad %ae %s", "--"],
        cwd=full_dir,
    ).rstrip()
    logs = re.sub(r"(?m)^(\d\d\d\d-\d\d-\d\d [^@]+)@[^ ]+( .*)$", r"\1\2", logs)
    lines = logs.splitlines()
    cleaned_lines = [l for l in lines if not _ROLL_SUBJECT.match(l)]  # noqa: E741
    logs = "\n".join(cleaned_lines) + "\n"

    nb_commits = len(lines)
    rolls = nb_commits - len(cleaned_lines)
    header = (
        f"Roll {dependency}/ {commit_range_for_header} "
        f"({nb_commits} commit{'s' if nb_commits > 1 else ''}"
        f"{f'; {rolls} trivial rolls' if rolls else ''})\n\n"
    )
```

```text
# The epoch is prepended to the version when constructing the version: tag
# for both the source package and the final built package. It must be
# incremented in the case of incompatible changes to the source package
# format, or any time that we need to force new builds of all packages.
PACKAGE_EPOCH = '2'
--- pkgbuild/pkg/spec/loader/loader.go ---
const cipdVersionEpoch = "3@"
--- pkgbuild/pkg/spec/loader/create.go ---
// CIPDVersion returns the version tag used in cipd.
func (p *createParser) CIPDVersion() string {
	if p.PatchVersion == "" {
		return cipdVersionEpoch + p.SourceVersion
	}
	return cipdVersionEpoch + p.SourceVersion + "." + p.PatchVersion
}
```

```python


def GetPlatformUrlPrefix(host_os):
  _HOST_OS_URL_MAP = {
    'linux': 'Linux_x64',
    'mac': 'Mac',
    'mac-arm64': 'Mac_arm64',
    'win': 'Win',
  }
  return CDS_URL + '/' + _HOST_OS_URL_MAP[host_os] + '/'


def DownloadAndUnpackPackage(
  package_file, output_dir, host_os, version=PACKAGE_VERSION
):
  cds_file = "%s-%s.tar.xz" % (package_file, version)
  cds_full_url = GetPlatformUrlPrefix(host_os) + cds_file
  try:
    DownloadAndUnpack(cds_full_url, output_dir)
  except urllib.error.URLError:
    print('Failed to download prebuilt clang package %s' % cds_file)
    print('Use build.py if you want to build locally.')
    print('Exiting.')
```

### X61. `src/tools/rust/update_rust.py`:161-185

*Shows (TP):* Standalone (non-gclient) path of update_rust.py: builds the URL rust-toolchain-<rev>-<sub>-<clang_rev>.tar.xz, skips if VERSION already matches, and honours the .*_is_first_class_gcs marker.

```python
    platform_prefix = GetPlatformUrlPrefix(GetDefaultHostOs())

    version = GetRustClangRevision()

    # Exit early if the existing package is up-to-date. Note that we cannot
    # simply call DownloadAndUnpack() every time: aside from unnecessarily
    # downloading the toolchain if it hasn't changed, it also leads to multiple
    # versions of the same rustlibs. build/rust/std/find_std_rlibs.py chokes in
    # this case.
    # .*_is_first_class_gcs file is created by first class GCS deps when rust
    # hooks are migrated to be first class deps. In case we need to go back to
    # using a hook, this file will indicate that the previous download was
    # from the first class dep and the dir needs to be cleared.
    if os.path.exists(output_dir):
        if version == GetStampVersion() and not glob.glob(
            os.path.join(output_dir, '.*_is_first_class_gcs')
        ):
            return 0

    if os.path.exists(output_dir):
        shutil.rmtree(output_dir)

    try:
        url = f'{platform_prefix}rust-toolchain-{version}.tar.xz'
        DownloadAndUnpack(url, output_dir)
```

### X63. `src/build/util/lastchange.py`:168-189

*Shows (TP):* How LASTCHANGE is computed: git log -1 (filtered by ^Change-Id: to skip local commits) plus the Cr-Commit-Position footer parsed from the commit object, giving '<hash>-<ref@{#N}>'.

```python
    git_args = ['log', '-1', '--format=%H %ct']
    if commit_filter is not None:
        git_args.append('--grep=' + commit_filter)

    git_args.append(start_commit)

    output = _RunGitCommand(directory, git_args)
    hash_, commit_timestamp = output.split()
    if not hash_:
        return _EMPTY_VERSION_INFO

    revision = hash_
    pos = ''
    output = _RunGitCommand(directory, ['cat-file', 'commit', hash_])
    for line in reversed(output.splitlines()):
        if line.startswith('Cr-Commit-Position:'):
            pos = line.rsplit()[-1].strip()
            logging.debug("Found Cr-Commit-Position '%s'", pos)
            revision = "{}-{}".format(hash_, pos)
            break
    return VersionInfo(hash_, revision, pos, int(commit_timestamp))
```

```python
        variables = self.get_vars()
        for arg in self._gn_args:
            if not isinstance(arg, str) or not gclient_eval.GN_ARG_REGEXP.match(
                arg
            ):
                raise gclient_utils.Error(
                    f"Invalid gclient_gn_args {arg!r}: Must be a valid GN identifier."
                )
            if arg not in variables:
                raise gclient_utils.Error(
                    f"Invalid gclient_gn_args: {arg!r} is not defined in vars."
                )
            value = variables[arg]
            if isinstance(value, gclient_eval.ConstantString):
                value = value.value
            elif isinstance(value, str):
                value = gclient_eval.EvaluateCondition(value, variables)
            lines.append(f"{arg} = {ToGNString(value)}")
```

### X85. `https://docs.google.com/document/d/1N_fseFNOj10ETZG3pZ-I30R__w96rYNtvx5y_jFGJWw/export?format=txt`:21-24, 139-142

*Shows (SM):* The cost of SUBMODULES mode as stated by its designers, and the three-state definition

```text
Breaking changes
1. No longer possible to point a git dependency to non-commit (e.g. branch or HEAD).
2. No longer possible to override hosts, repo, or commit hash using DEPS variables.
3. (indirect) DEPS file no longer contains git dependencies.
...
* DEPS -> Only use DEPS file for read/write (default).
* SYNC -> Keep DEPS and submodules in sync for write; assume they are in-sync for read. Useful intermediate state for migration.
* SUBMODULES -> Use only git submodules for read/write.
```

```text
### Why do we have Git dependencies in both DEPS and Git submodules?

Lots of Chromium infrastructure already parse DEPS file directly. Instead of a
massive switch, it's easier to transition to Git submodules this way. Moreover,
unwanted Git submodule updates can be detected and developers can be warned.
```

```python
  # Get the epoch of the git cache from a cache epoch marker file. If this file
  # does not exist, create one with the current timestamp.
  cache_epoch_marker_path = os.path.join(options.git_cache_dir, ".cache_epoch")
  if os.path.isfile(cache_epoch_marker_path):
    with open(cache_epoch_marker_path) as f:

  else:
    # This ensures the cache path exists. This is a noop if the path already

      print(cache_epoch, file=f)

  print("git_cache epoch: {}".format(datetime.fromtimestamp(int(cache_epoch))))
```

```python
def create_manifest():
  fd, fname = tempfile.mkstemp()
  os.close(fd)
  try:
    revinfo = call_gclient(  # noqa: F841
      "revinfo", "-a", "--ignore-dep-type", "cipd", "--output-json", fname
    )
    with open(fname) as f:
      return {
        path: {
          "repository": info["url"],
          "revision": info["rev"],
        }
        for path, info in json.load(f).items()
        if info["rev"] is not None
      }
  except (ValueError, SubprocessFailed):
    return {}
  finally:
    os.remove(fname)
```

```python
class CacheMode(enum.StrEnum):
    """How checkouts relate to the git cache when cache_dir is set."""

    # clone --shared, fetch URL stays on the mirror; the checkout only works
    # while the cache exists (bot topology).
    SHARED = "shared"

    # The mirror only seeds checkouts that do not exist yet (objects
    # hardlinked or copied, fetch URL on the real remote); the cache is
    # deletable.
    BOOTSTRAP = "bootstrap"


class GitWrapper(SCMWrapper):
    """Wrapper for Git"""

    name = "git"
    remote = "origin"

    cache_mode = CacheMode.SHARED
```

### X113. `src/docs/linux/build_instructions.md`:83-100

*Shows (QP):* the only official size/time claims for a checkout

````text
If you don't want the full repo history, you can save a lot of time by
adding the `--no-history` flag to `fetch`.

You can make this much faster by passing `--git-cache` to `fetch`, which
seeds the checkout from a shared, prebuilt snapshot instead of cloning from
scratch (and, unlike `--no-history`, keeps the full history):

```shell
$ fetch --git-cache chromium
```

The cache directory is chosen automatically (override with `$GIT_CACHE_PATH`).
It mirrors every repo it fetches (~30 GB for Chromium) and is shared by all
checkouts on the machine: working trees reference it instead of copying the
objects, so the per-checkout `.git` stays small.

Expect the command to take 30 minutes on even a fast connection, and many
hours on slower ones.
````

*Shows (QP):* definition behind '1639835' (depth of main's history on 2026-09-21)

```python
Calculates the generation number for one or more commits in a git repo.

Generation number of a commit C with parents P is defined as:
  generation_number(C, []) = 0
  generation_number(C, P)  = max(map(generation_number, P)) + 1
```

### X128. `depot_tools/gclient_eval.py`:588-609

*Shows (PH):* The 2026-tree code (from the 2018-05-16 CL) that turns any surviving deps_os into checkout_* conditions

```python
def _MergeDepsOs(deps_dict, os_deps_dict, os_name):
    """Merges the deps in os_deps_dict into conditional dependencies in deps_dict.

    The dependencies in os_deps_dict are transformed into conditional dependencies
    using |'checkout_' + os_name|.
    If the dependency is already present, the URL and revision must coincide.
    """
    for dep_name, dep_info in os_deps_dict.items():
        # Make this condition very visible, so it's not a silent failure.
        # It's unclear how to support None override in deps_os.
        if dep_info["url"] is None:
            logging.error(
                "Ignoring %r:%r in %r deps_os", dep_name, dep_info, os_name
            )
            continue

        os_condition = "checkout_" + (os_name if os_name != "unix" else "linux")
        UpdateCondition(dep_info, "and", os_condition)
```

### X130. `src/PRESUBMIT.py`:3341-3353

*Shows (PH):* The surviving .DEPS.git presubmit check in the 2026 tree

```python
def CheckNoDEPSGIT(input_api, output_api):
    """Make sure .DEPS.git is never modified manually."""
    if any(f.LocalPath().endswith('.DEPS.git')
           for f in input_api.AffectedFiles()):
        return [
            output_api.PresubmitError(
                'Never commit changes to .DEPS.git. This file is maintained by an\n'
                'automated system based on what\'s in DEPS and your changes will be\n'
                'overwritten.\n'
                'See https://sites.google.com/a/chromium.org/dev/developers/how-tos/'
                'get-the-code#Rolling_DEPS\n'
                'for more information')
        ]
    return []
```

### X131. `infra/goma/client@5de52a5ece34: README.md`:16-24

*Shows (GH):* The two mechanisms Goma offered: remote parallel compilation and backend result caching

```text
## How Goma works

Goma hooks a compile request, and sends it to a backend compile server.
If you have plenty of backend servers, a lot of compile can be processed in
parallel, for example, -j100, -j500 or -j1000.

Also, the Goma backend caches the compile result. If the same compile request
comes, the cached result is returned from the Goma cache server.
```

```cpp
    // running state, or state at response sent if abort_ is true.

    FILE_REQ,  // Upload input files.

    FILE_RESP,  // Download output files.
    // finished state:  response sent.
    FINISHED,  // Finished.

  };
```

```cpp
std::string HttpClient::Request::BuildHeader(
    const std::vector<std::string>& headers,
    int content_length) const {
  std::ostringstream msg;
  msg << method_ << " " << request_path_ << " HTTP/1.1\r\n";
  if (host_ != "") {
    msg << kHost << ": " << host_ << "\r\n";
  }
  msg << kUserAgent << ": " << kUserAgentString << "\r\n";
  msg << kContentType << ": " << content_type_ << "\r\n";
  if (content_length >= 0) {
    msg << kContentLength << ": " << content_length << "\r\n";
  }
  if (authorization_ != "") {
    msg << kAuthorization << ": " << authorization_ << "\r\n";
  }
  if (cookie_ != "") {
    msg << kCookie << ": " << cookie_ << "\r\n";
  }
```

*Shows (GH):* Content-addressed file transfer: sha256 keys, 2 MB embedding threshold, chunking of large inputs

```text
// hash_key = sha256(serialized FileBlob)
//
// for small file (< 2MB) embedded
//   blob_type=FILE, !has_offset(), has_content()
//                   has_file_size(), hash_key_size() == 0
//
// for large file
//   blob_type=FILE_META, !has_offset(), !has_content()
//                   has_file_size(), hash_key_size() > 0
//  for each hash_key(i)
//     blob_type=FILE_CHUNK, has_offset(), has_content(),
//                   has_file_size(), hash_key_size() == 0
//
// for small file (< 2MB), stored as blob_type=FILE in file server with
// key=hash_key[0]
//   blob_type=FILE_REF, !hash_offset(), !has_content()
//                   has_file_size(), hash_key_size() == 1
```

### X143. `depot_tools@443f9851a46a: autoninja.py`:190-212

*Shows (GH):* How autoninja turned a goma build into a -j of hundreds/thousands

```python
    if use_goma or use_remoteexec:
      args.append('-j')
      default_core_multiplier = 80
      if platform.machine() in ('x86_64', 'AMD64'):
        # Assume simultaneous multithreading and therefore half as many cores as
        # logical processors.
        num_cores //= 2

      core_multiplier = int(
          os.environ.get('NINJA_CORE_MULTIPLIER', default_core_multiplier))
      j_value = num_cores * core_multiplier

      core_limit = int(os.environ.get('NINJA_CORE_LIMIT', j_value))
      j_value = min(j_value, core_limit)

      if sys.platform.startswith('win'):
        # On windows, j value higher than 1000 does not improve build
        # performance.
        j_value = min(j_value, 1000)
      elif sys.platform == 'darwin':
        # On macOS, j value higher than 800 causes 'Too many open files' error
        # (crbug.com/936864).
        j_value = min(j_value, 800)

      args.append('%d' % j_value)
```

```python
def __disable_remote(ctx, step_config):
    gn_logs_data = gn_logs.read(ctx)
    if gn_logs_data.get("use_remoteexec") == "true":
        return step_config
    for rule in step_config["rules"]:
        rule["remote"] = False
    return step_config

def __unset_timeout(ctx, step_config):
    if not config.get(ctx, "no-remote-timeout"):
        return step_config
    for rule in step_config["rules"]:
        # if no timeout, default is 60m timeout.
        # better to keep longer timeout instead of using shorter timeout.
        timeout = rule.get("timeout")
        if timeout and \
           time.parse_duration(timeout) > time.parse_duration("60m"):
            continue
        rule.pop("timeout", None)
    return step_config
```

### X158. `src/build/config/siso/reclient.star`:18-41

*Shows (RS):* The hybrid mode: with use_reclient=true Siso delegates only clang compiles to rewrapper (use_remote_exec_wrapper) and disables its own native remote execution everywhere else.

```python
def __step_config(ctx, step_config):
    new_rules = []
    for rule in step_config["rules"]:
        if (rule["name"].startswith("clang/cxx") or rule["name"].startswith("clang/cc") or
            rule["name"].startswith("clang-cl/cxx") or rule["name"].startswith("clang-cl/cc") or
            rule["name"].startswith("clang/objc") or rule["name"].startswith("clang-coverage/")):
            # Enable remote exec wrapper.
            rule["use_remote_exec_wrapper"] = True
            rule["remote"] = False
            rule.pop("handler", None)

            # Remove command_prefix to match wrapped commands.
            rule.pop("command_prefix", None)

            new_rules.append(rule)
            continue

        # Disable native remote execution for other rules when using reclient.
        if rule.get("remote"):
            rule["remote"] = False
        new_rules.append(rule)

    step_config["rules"] = new_rules
    return step_config
```

```python
def _get_use_siso_default(output_dir):
    """Returns use_siso default value."""
    root_dir = gclient_paths.GetPrimarySolutionPath(output_dir)
    if not root_dir:
        return False

    # autoninja requires .sisoenv to set Siso env vars such as SISO_PROJECT
    # and SISO_REAPI_INSTANCE.
    sisoenv_path = os.path.join(root_dir, "build/config/siso/.sisoenv")
    if not os.path.exists(sisoenv_path):
        return False

    # Check the project wide default in `.gn`.
    dot_gn = os.path.join(root_dir, ".gn")
    if os.path.exists(dot_gn):
        with open(dot_gn) as f:
            dot_gn_lines = f.readlines()
        p = re.compile(r"(^|\s*)(use_siso)\s*=\s*(true)\s*$")
        if any(p.match(l) for l in dot_gn_lines):  # noqa: E741
            return True

    # Checking `build_with_chromium` var in //build/config/gclient_args.gni
    # to enable Siso on Chromium.
    # TODO: crbug.com/409223168 - Remove this condition after setting use_siso
    # in Chromium's .gn + some buffer.
```

### X164. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/build/+/refs/heads/main/siso/build/run_remote.go`:145-169

*Shows (RS):* Siso's built-in execution strategy for a remote-eligible step: start-local, cache lookup, fast-local, remote, retry, fallback.

```go
// runRemote runs step with using remote apis.
//
//  1. for initial steps of startLocal, run locally.
//  2. Check remote cache with deps log if available.
//  3. If local resource is idle, run locally.
//  4. Otherwise, try running a remote execution with deps log.
//  5. If it failed, it will retry a remote execution with deps scan.
//  6. If it still failed, it will fallback to local execution.
//
// - Before each remote exec, it checks remote cache before running.
// - The fallbacks can be disabled via experiment flags.
func (b *Builder) runRemote(ctx context.Context, step *Step) error {
	preprocErr := errNeedPreproc
	needCheckCache := true
	cacheCheck := b.cache != nil && b.reCacheEnableRead
	strictRemote := step.def.Binding("strict_remote") == "true"
	startLocal := !strictRemote && b.startLocalCounter.Add(-1) >= 0
	if startLocal {
		// no cacheCheck as startlocal for incremental build
		// will build modified code, and not expect cache hit (?)
		clog.Infof(ctx, "start local %s", step.cmd.Desc)
		err := b.execLocal(ctx, step)
		step.metrics.StartLocal = true
		return err
	}
```

```go
	// to protect from out of memory, or too many threads.
	stepLimitFactor = 512

	// limit # of concurrent scandeps steps at most 2 times of num cpus
	// to protect from out of memory, reduce contention
	scanDepsLimitFactor = 2

	// limit # of concurrent steps at most 80 times of num cpus
```

```text
// Compared with Goma's input processor, scandeps only supports simple
// form of C preprocessor directives and uses precomputed subtree
// for sysroots or complicated include dirs.
//
// Scandeps only checks the following forms of #include
//
//	#include "foo.h"
//	#include <foo.h>
//	#include FOO_H
//
// to support last case, it also checks the following forms of #define
//
//	#define FOO_H "foo.h"
//	#define FOO_H <foo.h>
//	#define FOO_H OTHER_FOO_H
//
// Since scandeps doesn't process `#if` or `#ifdef`, it expands all possible
// values of macros for `#include FOO_H`.  Using extra inputs is
// not problem, but may have potential cache miss issues, since
// there is discrepancy between simple scandeps vs clang's *.d outputs.
// TODO(b/283341125): fix cache miss issue.
```

### X168. `siso/scandeps/cpp.go`:160-191

*Shows (SI):* How '#include MACRO' is expanded to every value ever defined (no #if evaluation), and why function-like macros need the clang fallback

```go
func cppExpandMacros(ctx context.Context, paths []string, incname string, macros map[string][]string) ([]string, error) {
	if incname == "" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	if strings.Contains(incname, "(") {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("func macro %q: %w", incname, errUnsupportedMacro)
	}
	if !isMacro(incname) {
		// literal includes
		return append(paths, incname), nil
	}
	values, ok := macros[incname]
	if !ok {
		clog.Infof(ctx, "missing macro %q", incname)
		return paths, nil
	}
	var retErr error
	for _, v := range values {
		var err error
		paths, err = cppExpandMacros(ctx, paths, v, macros)
		if err != nil {
			retErr = err
		}
	}
```
